correctness.rationale: For perfect structure matrices the squared natural basis is independent; products of distinct images force a monomial isomorphism and the coefficient equation a_ij c_j = c_i^2 b_sigma(i),sigma(j). The fixed-field two-relation graph forces fiber rotations (all scalars c_i) and realizes this equation exactly; both implications are proven, including q=2. The incidence block matrix has determinant 1 in all characteristics, and indegree-one versus indegree-three nodes reconstruct the input graph. Fixed finite-colored relational isomorphism reduces to ordinary GI by polynomial incidence gadgets. Independent exhaustive finite checks and samples replay from check.py; no finite test is used to infer universal validity.

value.rationale: An exact fixed-field GI-completeness classification settles the core decision-complexity comparison of Question 50 for every finite field, not a sporadic example or table. The size n(q-1) graph encodes the otherwise troublesome scalar-gauge action efficiently. It yields both a useful algorithmic upper reduction and an explicit sparse, determinant-one GI-hard subclass, while distinguishing fixed-field complexity from field-as-input complexity.
